Complete guide

Dressmaker Game

Dressmaker is a cozy dressmaking simulator from developers elyaradine (Jonathan Hau-Yoon), sarandipityx (Sara Laubscher) and raithza (Ruan Rothmann), published by Free Lives under the Cozy Lives label. You run a small dress shop: take a commission, choose the fabric, lay out the pattern, cut it out, sew it together and decorate the finished dress. Then you hand it in and find out whether your customer loves it — or whether you have quietly ruined their wedding.

Dressmaker is a cozy dressmaking simulation where you take a commission, cut the pattern, sew the dress and hand it in. It released on Steam on September 21, 2026 for Windows and macOS at $14.99, and a free prototype is on itch.io.

What is Dressmaker?

A making game, not a shop-management game. Almost every minute happens at the table: cloth in front of you, pattern pieces in hand, deciding what goes where.

  • Your layout is permanent

    Where you place a pattern piece is exactly what shows on the finished dress. Nothing later undoes a bad cut.

  • Real dressmaking words

    Grain, bias, panels, appliqué. The game uses the real vocabulary and then shows you what it does.

  • You can be a menace

    The official pitch invites you to satisfy or sabotage your customers. Send the mayor's daughter out in clashing velvet if you like.

The loop, in five stages

Each stage is one decision and one cost. The full how to play Dressmaker walkthrough covers every screen.

  1. 1

    Read the commission

    the customer brings an occasion, a taste and a budget.

  2. 2

    Design in the sketchbook

    silhouette, colour, fabric samples, appliqué.

  3. 3

    Buy fabric and lay out the pattern

    each bolt has a print, a direction and a price.

  4. 4

    Cut, then sew

    cutting is permanent; the sewing machine has an infinite bobbin.

  5. 5

    Decorate and hand in

    buttons, bows and lace, then coin, reputation and a star rating.

Warning

cutting is the point of no return. Fabric is spent the moment the shears go through it.

How your dress is scored

A commission is not judged on vibes. The sketchbook lists named attributes with numeric targets, and your dress is measured against them.

Where you see itWhat it looks likeWhat it means
Sketchbook, Requirements boxQuality 70, Flowers 60, Cute 30, Romantic 45What this customer will judge you on
Sketchbook, budget800, and roughly 3.85m of fabricWhat you can afford to spend
Fabric shop, commission limitsQuality 0/80, Formal 0/50, Simple 0/75, Professional 0/50Progress against a ceiling
Fabric shop, hard rule"Use only black"Non-negotiable, beats taste
Customer card at hand-inA star ratingHow the dress landed, in stars

The developers have never published the full attribute list, so expect names to vary by client. Customer preferences covers how to read a brief.

Beginner tips

  1. 1

    Align the pattern to the grain

    bias cuts are a deliberate choice, not an accident.

  2. 2

    Keep big prints off small panels

    a large floral loses its shape on a bodice.

  3. 3

    Preview on the mannequin every time

    it is the last free check you get.

Tip

while you are learning, buy the cheapest cloth that meets the brief. Save silk and velvet for commissions that pay.

There is a longer list, including seam order and trim discipline, on the Dressmaker guide and sewing tips page.

Customers and rewards

You giveYou get
A dress that meets the briefCoin, reputation, a good star rating
A dress that misses the briefLess coin, and you will see it in the reaction
A dress sold off the rackSteady coin, with nobody's wedding depending on it

Reputation opens better commissions. The Dressmaker customer preferences page covers reading a brief and playing the sabotage run on purpose.

Frequently asked questions

  1. Is Dressmaker a real game or just a demo?

    Both exist, and they are separate builds. The free prototype on itch.io is a substantial slice that players have rated 4.8 out of 5. The paid Steam release is the full game, with story commissions, a town of clients, achievements and an ending.

  2. Is Dressmaker free?

    The itch.io prototype is free on a name-your-own-price basis. The full Steam release costs $14.99 in the US, with a 10% launch discount to $13.49.

  3. When did Dressmaker come out?

    Dressmaker released on Steam on September 21, 2026 for Windows and macOS. The free prototype has been on itch.io since 2025.

  4. Is this the same as DressMaker or DressMaker Pro on Steam?

    No, and it is worth knowing before you buy the wrong thing. There are two other games on Steam called DressMaker and DressMaker Pro, both released in 2021, and both are 3D character design tools rather than games. This page is about Dressmaker by Cozy Lives and Free Lives, the cozy dressmaking sim that released on September 21, 2026. If the store page you are looking at mentions character rigging or game development, you are on the wrong one.

  5. Is Dressmaker on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation or Xbox?

    Not yet. The released game is Windows and macOS on Steam, plus the Windows, macOS and Linux prototype on itch.io. In the launch-day Steam announcement the developers said they are planning mobile and Switch ports, so a console version is on the roadmap rather than available today.

  6. Is there a Dressmaker mobile app or a browser version I can play now?

    No playable mobile or browser version exists today, and we will not pretend otherwise. The developers did say on launch day that mobile ports are being planned, so expect an official announcement before any real app appears. Any site offering a "Dressmaker APK" or an online playable version right now is not affiliated with the developers.

  7. How long is Dressmaker?

    The developers describe roughly 35 hours of story commissions, before off-rack dresses, decorating for fun and the post-launch content they have said is still coming.

  8. Is Dressmaker made with AI?

    No. The developers have said the game is privately owned and made by hand, and the itch.io prototype carries the "No generative AI was used" tag. Art, code and music are credited to named people.

  9. Is Dressmaker hard?

    It is gentle by design — there is no timer and no fail state in the usual sense. The difficulty is that cutting is irreversible, so a careless layout costs fabric and coin. If you can plan a jigsaw, you can play Dressmaker.

  10. Where do I get Dressmaker?

    Buy it on Steam for Windows and macOS, or try the free prototype at elyaradine.itch.io/dressmaker. Both links go to the developers' own pages.
